title: Immunofluorescence Staining and Analysis of Microglial Cell Morphology in Mice
author: Lind-Holm Mogensen, Ameli, et al.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia and injection
steps.instruction: Weigh each mouse, calculate the injection volume, and prepare ketamine (100 mg/mL, Nimatek Vet) and medetomidine (1 mg/mL, Dorbene Vet) diluted in saline.

steps.title: Anesthetize and perfuse mouse
steps.instruction: Cover the mouse with paper, dim the light, and intraperitoneally inject the ketamine/medetomidine mixture. Clean the dissection table with Bacillol then 70 % ethanol, place three pieces of tissue paper (first on drip tray, second beside instruments, third to cover the mouse), assess reflexes, clean with ethanol, and when reflexes are absent perform a cardiac perfusion with cold PBS.

steps.title: Dissect brain
steps.instruction: Using forceps, bone trimmer and scissors, cut the skull as follows: (1) cut along the right intraparietal bone, (2) cut along the left intraparietal bone, (3) make a 5 mm midline cut and remove occipital and intraparietal bone, (4) cut along the midline to the frontal and nasal bones, (5) cut on the right between parietal and frontal bones to the eye sockets, (6) repeat on the left. Remove remaining bone without touching brain tissue, turn the head upside‑down, gently extract the brain and place it into a 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Hemisphere handling and fixation
steps.instruction: If only one hemisphere will be used for histology, wash the brain in cold PBS, cut it into two hemispheres with a rodent brain matrix, drop‑fix one hemisphere in cold 4 % PFA and keep at 4 °C for 24 h, and place the other hemisphere in PBS for downstream analyses. Store the brain (or hemispheres) on ice. Pause point: for whole‑brain morphology you may fix for 48 h; for one‑hemisphere use, keep the opposite hemisphere in the fridge for 24 h.

steps.title: Thaw tissue sections on slides
steps.instruction: Place glass slides with tissue sections on a piece of paper and defrost for 10 min.

steps.title: Day 1 – Wash, permeabilize and block
steps.instruction: Immerse slides in 1× PBS for 5 min twice. Then permeabilize and remove peroxidase by incubating in PBS containing 3 % H₂O₂ and 1.5 % Triton‑X‑100 for 30 min. Wash 1 × 5 min in PBS with 0.1 % Triton‑X‑100 and 1 × 5 min in 1× PBS. Block by immersing slides in 5 % BSA in PBS for 30 min, rinse, and blot excess liquid with KimWipes.

steps.title: Day 1 – Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate slides horizontally with 300 µL of 2 % BSA in 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100 containing primary antibody (dilution 1:1000) for 17 h overnight at room temperature. Cover the solution with Parafilm cut to cover the whole slide and place a water‑soaked paper tissue in the box to prevent drying.

steps.title: Day 2 – Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Gently remove Parafilm, inspect sections, then wash 3 × 10 min in 1× PBS 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100. Quickly dry slides, blot remaining liquid with KimWipes, add 300 µL of secondary antibody (1:1000) in 2 % BSA 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100, and incubate at room temperature for 2 h protected from light.

steps.title: Day 2 – Mounting
steps.instruction: Remove Parafilm, wash 3 × 10 min in 1× PBS, dry excess liquid with KimWipes, add one drop of DAPI‑containing mounting medium, place a glass coverslip, avoid bubbles (use cotton swabs if needed), let slides dry at room temperature for at least 2 h, then seal the coverslip to the Epredia slide with nail polish on each corner or side. Keep at room temperature for 12–18 h to ensure complete drying.

steps.title: Image acquisition and inspection
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑resolution 3‑D images of the stained sections. Open each acquisition in Imaris, inspect using Surpass and Slice View, and discard any acquisition with holes/ruptures, tile misalignment, dim signal in >4 stacks, or strongly uneven cell distribution.

steps.title: Imaris preprocessing
steps.instruction: Correct slice intensities with the Normalizer Layer, then apply a Gaussian Filter (width = 0.3) under Image Processing.

steps.title: Imaris segmentation of Iba1+ cells
steps.instruction: Use the Surface Creation Tool with the following settings: (a) Deselect ‘Classify Surfaces’ and ‘Object to Object Statistics’, press Next; (b) Select the Iba1 channel, enable Local Contrast (diameter = 0.5 µm) and Smooth (Surface Detail = 0.5 µm), press Next; (c) Set background subtraction threshold between 0.5 and 1.5, keep ‘Split Touching Object’ disabled, press Next; (d) Filter 3‑D structures by voxel size (typically 18 000–180 000 for mouse microglia at 20×), press Finish.

steps.title: Mask and export segmented image
steps.instruction: Select the created surface, open Edit, mask the segmentation to the Iba1 channel (voxel intensity outside surfaces = 0, inside = 255), delete all other channels (Edit → Delete Channels), and export the image in .ims format.

steps.title: Run MATLAB feature extraction
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB, load the FeatureExtract.m script from https://github.com/CorradoAmeliLU/MIC-MAC-2.1, set the input folder (segmented Imaris files), output folder, and the reprocess flag (TRUE or FALSE), then run the script. The script generates two files per acquisition: _attributes.mat (cell‑by‑cell morphological table) and _volumes.mat (logical 3‑D matrix of each cell).

steps.title: Data analysis and statistics
steps.instruction: Load the generated MATLAB files into your preferred analysis environment, perform morphological clustering (e.g., k‑means) or other statistical tests, remembering that the experimental unit is the animal and that cell‑level measurements should be averaged per animal before hypothesis testing. Choose parametric or non‑parametric tests based on normality and homoscedasticity, and consider regression models for multi‑factor experiments.

description: In fundamental and preclinical research, characterizing new animal models of human diseases and evaluating the efficacy of emerging drugs requires meticulous assessment techniques. Microglia morphology serves as an important metric in these efforts, serving not only as a marker for disease progression, but also as a key indicator of treatment response in the brain. This protocol outlines a detailed methodology aimed at quantifying microglial cell morphology at the single-cell level in situ. Through a combination of precise tissue handling, staining techniques and semi-automated imaging analyses, this protocol offers a comprehensive way to assess microglial morphological features, including number of processes, volume, and length of processes and clustering of various phenotypic shapes, such as compactness (e.g., amoeboid features). We previously used the fully automated pipeline in mouse and human post-mortem tissues.2,3 We recently adopted an optimized protocol to characterize the role of microglia in a DJ-1 deficient mouse model and to specifically assess the effect of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation in wild-type and DJ-1 knockout mice.1 This protocol adds solutions to troubleshooting steps for tissue handling, staining and analysis, helping in optimizing microglia analyses in situ in murine brain samples at a single cell level. Additionally, the usage of one hemisphere for morphological analyses allows conducting simultaneous -omics studies on the other hemisphere, including single-cell transcriptional analyses. By integrating these methodologies, researchers can obtain valuable insights into microglial phenotypic acquisition and dynamics using a limited number of animals. Furthermore, this protocol offers the option to cluster cells based on morphology and in parallel conduct complementary analyses of microglial cells or other CNS features from the same brain.
